title: Forces and Equilibrium Module 4 Lesson 1: Horizontal Friction Coefficient custom practice

evidence_basis.originality_note: All prompts, numerical values and physical configurations are original; mapped Cambridge past-paper evidence informs cognitive demand and assessment structure only.

parts.prompt: A box of mass $4\text{ kg}$ rests in limiting equilibrium on a rough horizontal floor under the action of a horizontal pulling force of $16\text{ N}$. Taking $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$, calculate the coefficient of friction $\mu$ between the box and the floor.

A crate of mass $10\text{ kg}$ rests on rough horizontal ground and is pulled by a force of magnitude $50\text{ N}$ inclined at an angle of $30^\circ$ above the horizontal. Taking $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$, calculate the magnitude of the normal reaction $R$ exerted by the ground on the crate.

A block of mass $6\text{ kg}$ rests on a rough horizontal table. A worker pushes the block with a force of magnitude $40\text{ N}$ directed downwards at an angle of $30^\circ$ below the horizontal. Taking $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$, calculate the magnitude of the normal reaction $R$ exerted by the table on the block.

A parcel of mass $5\text{ kg}$ rests on a rough horizontal floor where the coefficient of friction is $\mu = 0.3$. A horizontal pulling force of $12\text{ N}$ is applied to the parcel. Taking $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$, determine the actual frictional force $F_f$ acting on the parcel, and state whether the parcel moves.

A sled of mass $25\text{ kg}$ is pulled along horizontal snow at a constant velocity by a horizontal rope. The coefficient of dynamic friction between the sled and the snow is $\mu = 0.08$. Taking $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$, calculate the tension $T$ in the rope.

A heavy metal block of mass $8\text{ kg}$ rests on a rough horizontal workbench where the coefficient of friction is $\mu = 0.45$. Taking $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$, calculate the maximum horizontal force $P_{\max}$ that can be applied to the block without causing it to move.

questions.prompt: A crate of mass $m = 15\text{ kg}$ is pulled across a rough horizontal floor by a force of magnitude $P$ acting at an angle of $25^\circ$ above the horizontal. The crate moves at a constant speed, and the coefficient of friction between the crate and the floor is $\mu = 0.35$. Taking $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$:

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: By resolving forces vertically, express the normal reaction $R$ in terms of $P$.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: By applying the friction relationship for motion at constant speed, calculate the pulling force $P$ correct to 3 significant figures.

questions.prompt: A trunk of mass $m = 20\text{ kg}$ rests on a rough horizontal surface with coefficient of friction $\mu = 0.4$. Taking $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$ (weight $W = 200\text{ N}$):

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: A force $P_1$ pushes the trunk at an angle of $30^\circ$ below the horizontal. If the trunk is in limiting equilibrium, calculate the magnitude of $P_1$ correct to 3 significant figures.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Alternatively, a force $P_2$ pulls the trunk at an angle of $30^\circ$ above the horizontal. Calculate $P_2$ for limiting equilibrium, and explain why $P_2 < P_1$.

questions.prompt: A block $A$ of mass $m_A = 4\text{ kg}$ rests on a rough horizontal table. A light inextensible string attached to $A$ passes over a small smooth pulley fixed at the edge of the table and supports a vertically hanging mass $B$ of mass $m_B = 1.6\text{ kg}$. The system is in limiting equilibrium on the point of slipping. Taking $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$:

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Determine the tension $T$ in the string, and show that the coefficient of friction between block $A$ and the table is $\mu = 0.4$.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: An extra mass of $1.5\text{ kg}$ is placed on top of block $A$. Calculate the new maximum static frictional force, and explain why the system remains stationary.

questions.prompt: A heavy block of mass $m = 5\text{ kg}$ rests on a rough horizontal floor where the coefficient of friction is $\mu = 0.5$. Two horizontal forces act on the block simultaneously: a force of magnitude $16\text{ N}$ directed due East, and a force of magnitude $12\text{ N}$ directed due North. Taking $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$:

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Calculate the magnitude of the resultant applied horizontal force $P$, and determine the direction of this resultant force as a bearing correct to 1 decimal place.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Determine whether the block moves, and find the magnitude and bearing of the frictional force $F_f$ acting on the block.

questions.prompt: A small ring of mass $m = 0.3\text{ kg}$ is threaded on a rough fixed horizontal rod with coefficient of friction $\mu = 0.6$. A light inextensible string attached to the ring is pulled with tension $T = 5\text{ N}$ at an angle $\theta$ above the horizontal. Taking $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$ (weight $W = 3\text{ N}$):

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: When $\theta = 20^\circ$, calculate the normal reaction $R$ exerted by the rod on the ring and find the maximum possible frictional force $F_{\max}$, giving each value correct to 3 significant figures.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Calculate the horizontal pulling component of the string tension when $\theta = 20^\circ$, and deduce whether the ring remains in equilibrium or accelerates along the rod.

parts.label: (c)
parts.prompt: Find the critical angle $\theta_c$ above the horizontal such that the vertical component of the string tension completely lifts the ring off the rod ($R = 0$).

questions.prompt: A heavy crate of mass $M = 40\text{ kg}$ rests on a rough horizontal floor where the coefficient of friction is $\mu = 0.75$. A rope attached to the crate pulls with tension $T$ at an angle $\theta$ above the horizontal ($0^\circ \leqslant \theta < 90^\circ$). Taking $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$ (weight $W = 400\text{ N}$):

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt:
Show that for limiting equilibrium, the required tension $T$ is given by:
$$T = \frac{\mu W}{\cos\theta + \mu\sin\theta} = \frac{300}{\cos\theta + 0.75\sin\theta}$$

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: By expressing the denominator in the form $R_0\cos(\theta - \alpha)$, determine the optimal angle $\theta_{\text{opt}}$ that minimizes the required pulling force, and calculate the minimum tension $T_{\min}$.

questions.prompt: Two blocks $A$ (mass $m_A = 6\text{ kg}$) and $B$ (mass $m_B = 4\text{ kg}$) rest on a rough horizontal floor connected by a light inextensible horizontal string. The coefficient of friction between block $A$ and the floor is $\mu_A = 0.3$, and between block $B$ and the floor is $\mu_B = 0.5$. A horizontal force $P$ is applied to block $B$ pulling it directly away from block $A$. Taking $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$:

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Calculate the maximum static frictional force that can be mobilized on block $A$ and on block $B$.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: If the pulling force is $P = 15\text{ N}$, determine the tension $T$ in the connecting string, the friction force $F_A$ on block $A$, and the friction force $F_B$ on block $B$.

parts.label: (c)
parts.prompt: Determine the range of values of $P$ for which the connecting string is under non-zero tension while the two-block system remains in equilibrium, and state the maximum force $P_{\max}$ before slipping occurs.
